messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — I'm proposing a compact, hierarchical sidebar that flattens some project-level pages into grouped anchors to reduce click depth. Main goal: fewer levels, more predictable deep links for external tooling. Thoughts?

Aj Patel: +1 to predictability. We should define a canonical URL for each logical 'view' and a deterministic redirect when a legacy URL is used. That makes integrations and saved links reliable.

Kevin O'Neal: Quick UX nit — if we collapse things into groups, breadcrumbs become more important. I sketched a pattern where breadcrumbs show the logical path, while the sidebar highlights the root group. Example: Projects / Billing / Usage -> sidebar shows Projects > Billing (group expanded).

Dana R.: Accessibility: please ensure grouped anchors are implemented as real <nav> landmarks and support skip links. Keyboard nav must move focus into expanded groups predictably (no surprise jumps). Also check contrast for group headers — smaller targets = bigger a11y risk.

Maria Chen: Good call, Dana. I'll add skip link and landmark requirements. Aj — can you draft a short routing contract we can use to keep deep links stable? Needs to cover: canonical slugs, legacy redirects, and query param tolerance.

Aj Patel: Draft below — open to edits.

```
# Routing contract (proposal)
- /projects/:projectId/overview -> canonical overview
- /projects/:projectId/settings -> canonical settings (legacy: /projects/:projectId/config -> 301)
- /projects/:projectId/billing[:tab] -> supports ?tab=usage for deep linking but preserves canonical /billing
- group anchors: /projects/:projectId#deployments -> scroll anchor; also support /projects/:projectId/deployments for direct nav
- deep link fallback: if path unknown but projectId present -> redirect to /projects/:projectId/overview
```

Kevin O'Neal: That looks good. For breadcrumbs, prefer the humanized label instead of raw slug (e.g., "Team Alpha" not "team-alpha") — resolve labels from model cache to avoid extra roundtrips.

DesignBot: Prototype uploaded: https://figma.com/proto/redwood/compact-sidebar-v2 (comments enabled) :zap:

Pete Morales: We should run an experiment on discoverability before rolling everywhere. Two cohorts: A) group anchors (compact) B) current nested sidebar. Track: time-to-task (open billing, find usage), deep-link success rate, and keyboard shortcut adoption.

Maria Chen: Agreed. I'll own the experiment plan. Next steps: 1) finalize routing contract (Aj), 2) update accessibility checklist (Dana + Maria), 3) prototype comments resolved (everyone), 4) define metrics and rollout windows (Pete).

Aj Patel: I'll push an updated routing doc by EOD and add a small script to emit 301s for legacy paths in the edge layer.

Dana R.: I'll add aria-landmark examples and keyboard flow tests to the a11y doc.

Kevin O'Neal: FYI — small copy tweak: group header text should be verbs for actions ("Manage" instead of "Management") to make affordances clearer.

Maria Chen: Love that. Good microcopy callout, Kevin. I'll update the prototype and sticky notes.

Pete Morales: Ping me when the metrics spreadsheet is ready and I'll hook it into Amplitude experiments.

Maria Chen: Thanks all — let's reconvene after the prototype comments are resolved. :handshake:
